segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: Good morning, good morning, everyone, and welcome to our regular lecture on health issues.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: This series of lectures is organised by the Students’ Union and is part of the union’s attempt to help you, the students of this university, to stay healthy while coping with study and social life at the same time.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: So it’s a great pleasure for me to welcome back Ms Diane Greenbaum who is a professional dietician and who has been kind enough to give up her time, in what I know is a very hectic schedule, to come along and talk to us today.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Thank you.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Thank you very much, John.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: May I say it’s a pleasure to be back.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Now, stresses at university, being away from home and having to look after yourselves, learning your way around the campus all contribute to making it quite hard sometimes to ensure that your diet is adequate.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: So today I’m going to talk about ways of making sure that you eat well while at the same time staying within your budget.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: If you have a well balanced diet, then you should be getting all the vitamins that you need for normal daily living.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: However sometimes we think we’re eating the right foods but the vitamins are escaping, perhaps as a result of cooking and anyway we’re not getting the full benefit of them.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Now, if you lack vitamins in any way the solution isn’t to rush off and take vitamin pills. though they can sometimes help.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: No it’s far better to look at your diet and how you prepare your food.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: So what are vitamins?

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Well, the dictionary tells us they are food factors essential in small quantities to maintain life.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Now, there are fat soluble vitamins which can be stored for quite some time by the body and there are water soluble vitamins which are removed more rapidly from the body and so a regular daily intake of these ones is needed.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: OK, so how can you ensure that your diet contains enough of the vitamins you need?

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Well, first of all, you may have to establish some new eating habits!

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: No more chips at the uni canteen, I'm afraid!

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Now firstly, you must eat a variety of foods.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Then you need to ensure that you eat at least four servings of fruit and vegetables daily.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Now you'll need to shop two or three times a week to make sure that they're fresh, and store your vegetables in the fridge or in a cool dark place.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Now let s just refresh our memories by looking at the Healthy Diet Pyramid.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: OK, can you all see that?

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Good.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Well ,now, as you see we've got three levels to our pyramid.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: At the top in the smallest area are the things which we should really be trying to avoid as much as possible.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Things like Example yes, sugar, salt, butter all that sort of thing.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Next, on the middle of our pyramid we find the things that we can eat in moderation.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Not too much though!

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: And that's where we find milk, lean meat, fish, nuts, eggs.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: And then at the bottom of the pyramid are the things that you can eat lots of!

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: Because they're the things that are really good for you And here we have bread, vegetables and fruit.

segments.speaker: DIANE GREENBAUM
segments.en: So don't lose sight of your healthy diet pyramid when you do your shopping.
